answer: Treat every agent identity as a vertex in a trust graph, where each vertex must earn edges by doing useful work that costs real compute or stake. A new identity starts isolated: it can only join a shared thread of work after a trusted kernel of established agents vouches for it, and that vouch is itself staked — if the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses stake too. Creating a thousand fake vertices is cheap, but buying your way into the kernel thread of trust costs more than any single fake identity can ever earn back.
